title: Forecasting GPU Performance for Deep Learning Training and Inference
note: NeuSight predicts DL training/inference latency on unseen GPUs from tile-level models - pure user-space Python, needs only small profiling runs

title: MELF: Multivariant Executables for a Heterogeneous World
note: Purely binary-level (linker plus loader) mechanism for per-function, per-thread compile-time variants; the case studies are SQLite, memcached and MariaDB, all user-space workloads this machine runs well. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the heterogeneous-ISA case study assumes CPUs with differing extension sets - on a single Threadripper the ISA-adaptation experiment can only be emulated, so an improvement would have to target the security/debug-instrumentation isolation use case.

title: Improving Graph Compression for Efficient Resource-Constrained Graph Analytics
note: rule-based graph compression that cuts peak memory during both compression and computation; CPU only

title: VLCs: Managing Parallelism with Virtualized Libraries
note: Virtual Library Contexts partition library resources inside one process via custom dynamic linking - no kernel, no root, no special hardware. Benchmarks are OpenMP, OpenBLAS and LibTorch on a single node, which this 16-core machine can run. Concern - likely needs a recent clang/LLVM, installable per-user through conda.

title: Keyformer: KV Cache reduction through key tokens selection for Efficient Generative Inference
note: KV-cache eviction policy (key-token selection) for decode-phase memory/bandwidth - exactly the llm-inference topic and single-GPU by nature. Concern - accuracy evaluation on long-context summarization benchmarks costs GPU hours; 7B-class models only.

title: AWARE: Workload-aware, Redundancy-exploiting Linear Algebra
note: Workload-aware lossless compression for linear algebra inside Apache SystemDS; single-node CPU ML runtime with clear performance hypotheses. Concern: code lives in the large SystemDS codebase rather than a standalone artifact

title: 8-bit Transformer Inference and Fine-tuning for Edge Accelerators
note: Software FP8/Posit8 quantization-emulation library for Transformer inference and LoRA fine-tuning. Concern - Ampere has no native FP8 so numerics are emulated (which is what the artifact does anyway); the accompanying edge accelerator hardware results are out of reach.

title: Kepler: Robust Learning for Parametric Query Optimization
note: Learned parametric query optimization with row-count evolution and SNGP confidence - ML-based tuning with a released artifact and Postgres integration

title: Morphing-based Compression for Data-centric ML Pipelines
note: Pushes lossless matrix compression through feature transformations in data-centric ML pipelines inside SystemDS; memory and I O reduction work that runs on CPU. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/damslab/reproducibility/tree/master/vldb2026-BWARE .

title: GRACE: A Scalable Graph-Based Approach to Accelerating Recommendation Model Inference
note: Graph-based acceleration of recommendation-model inference on one CPU/GPU node - GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Self-Enhancing Video Data Management System for Compositional Events with Large Language Models
note: Video data management system that generates and distills UDF models; single-GPU vision models plus LLM API

title: FicusDB: Scalable Multi-Versioned Authenticated Archival Storage
note: Log-structured multi-versioned archival storage engine for copy-on-write tries with an Ethereum StateDB replay harness - single-node user-space storage engine, implementation is in the artifact repo

title: Mohabi: Disaggregating and Sandboxing the Firefox JavaScript Engine
note: Pure user-space software fault isolation of SpiderMonkey inside Firefox; no root, no kernel, single machine. Concerns: building Firefox plus a custom SFI/WASM toolchain is a heavy build (clang/LLVM must be installed per-user via conda, tens of GB of disk); browser benchmarking is noisy on a shared machine

title: WiseGraph: Optimizing GNN with Joint Workload Partition of Graph and Operations
note: GNN training framework with a joint graph/operator partitioning abstraction (gTask). The paper reports separate single-GPU numbers (2.04x) alongside multi-GPU, so the mechanism has a genuine single-GPU meaning. Concern - the largest graphs in the paper may not fit 24 GB, so a smaller dataset subset is needed

title: Meep Hashing: Ultrafast and Compact Minimal Perfect Hashing for Practical Large-Scale Lookup Systems
note: minimal perfect hashing with integrated alien-key filtering for large-scale lookup systems - small user-space data-structure library - concern: no repo located

title: CrossMapping: Harmonizing Memory Consistency in Cross-ISA Binary Translation
note: Memory-consistency primitive mapping in QEMU dynamic binary translation; QEMU TCG needs no KVM and no root, and the ARMv8-to-x86 and RISC-V-to-x86 directions run on our x86 host with PARSEC. Concern: the x86-to-ARMv8 and x86-to-RISC-V directions need ARM or RISC-V hosts we do not have, so only half the configuration matrix is reachable

title: FLEA: Frequency-based Lossless Encoding Algorithm for Periodic Time Series
note: frequency-based lossless encoder for periodic time series - compression artifact, CPU only - concern: domain-specific and no repo located

title: A House United Within Itself: SLO-Awareness for On-Premises Containerized ML Inference Clusters via Faro
note: SLO-aware cross-job resource allocation for ML inference driven by production traces; the optimizer and predictor are user-space Python. Concern - the reference stack is Ray Serve on Kubernetes and there is no root or Docker here, so the k8s layer must be replaced by a local Ray cluster or the paper's trace-driven simulator

title: ContTune: Continuous Tuning by Conservative Bayesian Optimization for Distributed Stream Data Processing Systems
note: ML-based configuration tuning - conservative Bayesian Optimization plus a Big-small decomposition that picks per-operator parallelism for Flink jobs, compared against DS2. The tuner itself is user-space Java and the search-quality hypothesis (fewer reconfigurations, no SLA violation) can be tested against the same baselines. Concern: the paper's setup is Flink 1.13 with 45 TaskManagers across three 48-core machines (max parallelism 90); our 16-core/32-thread node cannot reproduce that scale. Flink runs fine as a local multi-process cluster, so the experiment must be scaled down (fewer slots, smaller source rates) or driven by the paper's workload replay - this is the main risk and is flagged for the audit stage rather than being a hard blocker. [PVLDB 16(13), added from the vldbgap-2024 shard]

title: Gemel: Model Merging for Memory-Efficient, Real-Time Video Analytics at the Edge
note: Model merging to cut GPU memory for concurrently served edge vision models - a pure user-space memory-management question that fits one 24 GB GPU - Concern: the target is memory-starved edge boxes so the memory budget has to be deliberately constrained on an A5000 and the repo is a research prototype

title: RAP: Resource-aware Automated GPU Sharing for Multi-GPU Recommendation Model Training and Input Preprocessing
note: Co-running DLRM input preprocessing with training on the same GPU via resource-aware kernel fusion. Concern - paper is multi-GPU, but the co-running cost model and horizontal fusion are per-GPU and can be studied on one A5000.

title: Efficient LLM Serving for Agentic Workflows: A Data Systems Perspective
note: workflow-aware LLM serving with proactive KV/prompt caching and cache-aware scheduling, compared against vLLM - squarely an inference-serving system - concern: no repo located

title: SIMPLE: Efficient Temporal Graph Neural Network Training at Scale with Dynamic Data Placement
note: Temporal GNN training system with dynamic data placement between CPU and GPU; single-node. Concern: no repo found in GitHub search, repo unknown

title: VQPy: An Object-Oriented Approach to Modern Video Analytics
note: Python front-end plus an extensible backend that builds and optimizes video-analytics pipelines (detector/tracker cascades, frame filtering) - entirely user space, one GPU. Concern - reproducing the query set needs public video datasets and YOLO-class weights; gains are pipeline-optimization gains, so a hypothesis must be framed around the backend optimizer.

title: Zeus: Understanding and Optimizing GPU Energy Consumption of DNN Training
note: Energy-vs-time tradeoff for recurring DNN training jobs measured with just-in-time profiling on a single GPU - Concern: setting GPU power limits through NVML normally requires root so only the batch-size and job-level knobs may be reachable without the Zeus daemon - repo moved from SymbioticLab/Zeus to ml-energy/zeus

title: BaCO: A Fast and Portable Bayesian Compiler Optimization Framework
note: Bayesian autotuner for compiler/scheduling search spaces (TACO RISE HPVM) - pure user-space Python on one CPU/GPU node  open source

title: Compass: Encrypted Semantic Search with High Accuracy
note: ORAM + graph-index co-design; client and server are ordinary user-space processes and the paper's own workloads are embedding datasets that fit in 125 GiB RAM / 257 GB disk. Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: "various network conditions" results were obtained across machines - on one host they must be emulated with loopback delay (tc needs root, so an application-level delay injector is required instead).

title: Prism: Cost-Efficient Multi-LLM Serving via GPU Memory Ballooning
note: Elastic KV-cache memory ballooning across co-served models; the balloon driver (kvcached) is released and actively maintained, and multi-model co-serving on a single 24 GB GPU is the interesting regime. Concern: production evaluation uses many GPUs and bursty multi-model traces

title: LESS is More for I/O-Efficient Repairs in Erasure-Coded Storage
note: Repair-friendly erasure code construction reducing both bytes read and I/O seeks; the coding core is a user-space library (ISA-L based) and the trade-off can be studied with local microbenchmarks. Concern: end-to-end numbers come from HDFS on a local cluster - here that means a pseudo-distributed / multi-process HDFS on one host, which changes the network/seek balance.

title: Femur: A Flexible Framework for Fast and Secure Querying from Public Key-Value Store
note: Learned-index-based key-value retrieval framework with tunable security; user-space, single machine

title: The Case for DBMS Live Patching
note: user-space live patching of DBMS binaries via libpulp; no kernel module needed. Concern: confirm that the patching path works without extra privileges

title: Can Learned Indexes be Built Efficiently? A Deep Dive into Sampling Trade-offs
note: Sampling trade-offs for building learned indexes efficiently; CPU only. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search

title: Shaving the Peaks: Taming Tail Latency for Managed Workloads via Disaggregated Garbage Collection
note: Moves GC work off the mutator's CPU budget to cut tail latency in multi-tenant JVM workloads; single-server, user-space JVM/runtime work, and cgroup v2 cpu/memory controllers are delegated here. Concerns: artifact asks for a dual-socket NUMA Intel server with hyper-threading **disabled** (needs root) and assumes 32 physical cores per socket; this machine is single-socket, 16 cores

title: LeaseGuard: Raft Leases Done Right
note: Raft leader-lease algorithm with a Python simulator and a LogCabin C++ implementation - the simulator and single-host multi-process runs make it feasible - concern: no official repo confirmed

title: On-site, Non-speculative Failure Diagnosis with CLODS
note: On-site non-speculative failure diagnosis (YScope and U. Toronto - the CLP log-compression group, which has a track record of open-sourcing). User-space log and diagnosis tooling needs no root. Concern: no abstract or artifact public yet and the evaluation likely targets production distributed services.

title: Learned Static Function Data Structures
note: Learned static function data structures that use per-key predicted distributions to beat the zero-order entropy bound; pure user-space C++ library

title: CDMPP: A Device-Model Agnostic Framework for Latency Prediction of Tensor Programs
note: Learned cost model for tensor-program latency - a classic learned-component-inside-a-system paper. The released figshare dataset means the expensive cross-device profiling does not have to be redone; training the predictor fits one A5000. Concern - reproducing cross-device claims needs their published traces, not new hardware

title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
note: Checkpointing/fault tolerance specialised for MoE training; the partial-experts checkpoint idea can be scaled down to one GPU; concerns: motivated by 10k-node training and no official repo was found

title: Holistic and Automated Task Scheduling for Distributed LSM-tree-based Storage
note: HATS co-schedules foreground reads and background compaction in Cassandra; Java user-space prototype, no kernel or special hardware. Concern: it is a distributed KV store - a cluster must be emulated as several Cassandra JVMs on this one host (16 cores / 125 GiB is enough for a 3-5 node ring), and replica-selection results will be less faithful than on real nodes.

title: SANDHI: Fine-grained Merging for Memory Efficient Multi-Model Serving
note: Fine-grained merging of model weights to serve several models in less GPU memory. Memory-efficient multi-model serving on one 24 GB GPU is precisely this machine. Concern: no preprint or artifact found yet.

title: SPACE: Cardinality Estimation for Path Queries Using Cardinality-Aware Sequence-based Learning
note: Learned sequence-based cardinality estimator for path queries

title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
note: Customizable attention engine with block-sparse KV layouts and JIT templates - single GPU, Ampere supported, integrated into vLLM/SGLang so both baselines and improvement targets are easy - concern: some kernels are tuned for Hopper

title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
note: Hierarchical KV-cache manager on top of vLLM that classifies KV heads as stable or unstable and offloads cold pages to host memory; explicitly aimed at cutting GPU memory. Single GPU plus large host RAM is the ideal setup, and there is a Zenodo-archived artifact

title: Loupe: Driving the Development of OS Compatibility Layers
note: Dynamic syscall-usage analysis for OS compatibility layers; user-space ptrace/seccomp tooling plus a public results database. Concern - upstream harness wraps runs in Docker so it must be ported to a conda/bwrap setup.

title: Mint: Cost-Efficient Tracing with All Requests Collection via Commonality and Variability Analysis
note: Trace-volume reduction via commonality/variability analysis, works offline over production trace data; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: ACALSim: A Scalable Parallel Simulation Framework for High-Performance System Design Space Exploration
note: Parallel discrete-event simulation framework in ~26k lines of C++ aimed explicitly at single-node multi-core scaling - the 16-core/32-thread Threadripper is the paper's own target class. Clear improvement hypotheses around thread management and synchronization. Concern: the reference repo ships a Docker workspace, so deps must be installed by hand

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
note: Adaptive draft length, confidence-prior verification and an SLO-aware efficiency estimator - all scheduling logic inside a single-GPU serving loop. Draft plus target model pair fits 24 GB. Ampere supports FlashAttention-2 so no FP8 dependence. Concern - trace replay assumes a certain request rate, may need rescaling.

title: Aker: Density-Aware Approximate Caching for Vector Search
note: Approximate cache for disk-based vector search with a density-adaptive hit predicate and a staleness-bounded refresh mechanism integrated into pgvector; a genuine cache admission and consistency contribution

title: LiquidCache: Efficient Pushdown Caching for Cloud-Native Data Analytics
note: Pushdown cache layer that transcodes Parquet into a Liquid format to cut cache CPU time; built on Apache DataFusion in Rust. Cache and compute servers are separate processes and can both run on this host

title: Predictive and Near-Optimal Sampling for View Materialization in Video Databases
note: Predictive frame sampling for view materialization in video analytics; multi-object tracking models run on a single GPU. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference Efficiency through Block Dependency Analysis
note: BlockDepend adds block-level dependency analysis to an ML compiler for inter-operator fusion on one GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: MadEye: Boosting Live Video Analytics Accuracy with Adaptive Camera Configurations
note: Live video analytics that adapts PTZ camera orientation; the released repo is trace-driven simulation code plus collected per-orientation datasets, and server-side inference (YOLO-class models) fits the A5000. Concerns: original setup needs physical PTZ cameras and Mahimahi link emulation (Mahimahi needs setuid/root), so work must stay inside the released simulator; datasets are hosted on Dropbox which is an availability risk.

title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
note: Exo 2 user-schedulable scheduling language for high-performance kernels - user-space compiler, CPU targets, 80+ kernels as benchmarks

title: On the Limitations of Carbon-Aware Temporal and Spatial Workload Shifting in the Cloud
note: Trace/simulation study of carbon-aware batch and interactive workload scheduling across 123 regions; the released artifact is a simulator plus carbon-intensity data, so it runs on CPU alone. Concern - it is a limitations study rather than a system, so it suits the "improve the policy / add nuance" angle more than a pure speedup project

title: LLFree: Scalable and Optionally-Persistent Page-Frame Allocation
note: Allocator design (lock- and log-free, cache-friendly, anti-fragmentation) is squarely in the memory topic, and the core LLFree implementation is a standalone Rust library benchmarked in user space; 16C/32T is enough to show the scaling claims. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the strongest claims (beating Linux's buddy allocator, memory-compaction page-movement counts) require the patched-kernel variant, which is impossible without root - a project here is limited to the user-space allocator benchmarks.

title: RT: Regular Types for the Streaming Shell
note: Overlay type system for shell stream programs; artifact appendix gives the GitHub repo, checking is CPU-only and user space, and the evaluation corpus is hundreds of public shell programs. Concern: contribution is static checking, so "performance improvement" would have to mean checking speed, precision, or coverage

title: DTC-SpMM: Bridging the Gap in Accelerating General Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Tensor Cores
note: Tensor-core SpMM formats, reordering and pipelining; single modern NVIDIA GPU. Ampere tensor cores are supported.

title: OLAP on Modern Chiplet-Based Processors
note: chiplet-aware task placement for query engines; the target machine is a multi-CCD Threadripper PRO so the effect is present. Concern: part of the analysis relies on hardware counters that are blocked

title: Analysis and Evaluation of Using Microsecond-Latency Memory for In-Memory Indices and Caches in SSD-Based Key-Value Stores
note: analysis of microsecond-latency secondary memory for in-memory indices and caches of SSD-based KV stores with user-level prefetching - memory-tiering study done in user space - concern: original setup emulates a special memory device

title: Optimizing Datalog for the GPU
note: GPUlog single-GPU Datalog engine with the HISA data structure - user-space CUDA; concern: repo is the authors' GPU-Datalog line (GDlog) so the exact ASPLOS-25 artifact branch needs checking, and some datasets need >24 GB

title: Swan: Hybrid MVCC Management for Efficient Transaction Processing in LSM-Tree-Based Key-Value Stores
note: Hybrid in-memory and out-of-memory MVCC for LSM-based key-value stores with transaction-aware data separation and concurrent memtable flushing; single-node storage engine

title: Reducing the GPU Memory Bottleneck with Lossless Compression for ML
note: Lossless compression of ML tensors to cut PCIe transfer time - single GPU plus PCIe is exactly the setting this machine has, artifact available. Strong fit

title: RaBitQ: Quantizing High-Dimensional Vectors with a Theoretical Error Bound for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Vector quantization with error bounds for ANN search; CPU/SIMD only, very reproducible

title: Graph-Based Vector Search: An Experimental Evaluation of the State-of-the-Art
note: Experimental evaluation and unified framework for graph-based vector search; concern - largest datasets are 1B vectors, would need scale-down

title: Nemo: A Low-Write-Amplification Cache for Tiny Objects on Log-Structured Flash Devices
note: Set-associative flash-cache design built as a CacheLib module; runs in user space on the local NVMe drives

title: LM-Tree: A Hybrid Learned Index for Similarity Search in Metric Spaces
note: hybrid learned index for similarity search in metric spaces - a learned index structure, CPU only - concern: metric-space/similarity focus and no repo located

title: A Learned Cuckoo Filter for Approximate Membership Queries over Variable-sized Sliding Windows on Data Streams
note: Learned cuckoo filter for approximate membership over sliding windows - a learned filter inside a stream engine. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search

title: Verifying maximum link loads in a changing world
note: Velo is a Rust CPU-only verification prototype (repo URL in the paper) whose evaluation is "generate raw data, then post-process with Python"; runtime and memory on large ISP topologies are the metrics, both improvable on this machine. Concerns: the authors state the industrial case study cannot be released, so only the public-topology experiments are reproducible; Rust must be installed in user space (it is not preinstalled).

title: XSched: Preemptive Scheduling for Diverse XPUs
note: Preemption/scheduling framework implemented as a user-space shim over the accelerator command-queue API (CUDA driver level); artifact repo plus a separate xsched-artifacts repo and a Zenodo DOI; Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: the paper's generality claim spans ten XPUs - only one NVIDIA Ampere GPU is available here, and the highest hardware-preemption level may require capabilities the A5000 or driver 535 does not expose.

title: ParaRC: Embracing Sub-Packetization for Repair Parallelization in MSR-Coded Storage
note: The core contribution is an algorithmic one - a heuristic that trades repair bandwidth against maximum per-node repair load in MSR codes - and the bandwidth/load trade-off curve can be studied purely by simulation on one machine. Concern: the released prototype is a distributed repair system whose end-to-end numbers come from a ~10-node cluster over a real network. On this machine it would have to run as multiple processes on one host, so absolute degraded-read and full-node-recovery times will be distorted; the defensible experiments are the load-balancing heuristic and simulated repair schedules.

title: LIT: Lightning-fast In-memory Temporal Indexing
note: In-memory temporal index; CPU and RAM only

title: UniCache: Unifying Prefix Cache Eviction for Heterogeneous LLM Serving Workloads
note: Prefix KV-cache eviction policy for LLM serving. Trace-driven prefix-cache simulator plus a vLLM implementation - both run on one 24 GB GPU with a 7-8B model. Ideal improvement target: swap in a better eviction policy and re-run the simulator

title: A Case Study for Ray Tracing Cores: Performance Insights with BFS and Triangle Counting in Graphs
note: Repurposes GPU RT cores (OptiX BVH + ray casting) for graph BFS, triangle counting and set intersection, compared against CUDA baselines. Single GPU, user space, CUDA code in the repo. Our RTX A5000 is Ampere (CC 8.6) and does have 2nd-gen RT cores plus OptiX support, so the mechanism reproduces. Concerns: the paper's result is largely negative (RT cores lose to CUDA except at high skew), which suits the "reproduction with nuance" fallback; OptiX version may want a newer driver than 535, and large graphs must fit in 24 GB.

title: RECom: A Compiler Approach to Accelerating Recommendation Model Inference with Massive Embedding Columns
note: Compiler that fuses massive embedding-column subgraphs for recommendation inference on one GPU - open source from Alibaba

title: Tidehunter: Large-Value Storage With Minimal Data Relocation
note: WAL-as-permanent-storage key-value engine with lock-free writes on NVMe; production-quality Rust artifact. Concern: the 1 TB dataset experiment must be scaled down to the free space available

title: SwiftGS: Algorithm and System Co-Optimization for Fast 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
note: Single-GPU 3D Gaussian Splatting co-optimization (adaptive early sorting, axis-shared rasterization, dynamic thresholding) against the gsplat baseline, with code and a Zenodo benchmark archive. Ampere is a supported target

title: CloudGlide: Deconstructing the Landscape of Cloud-Based Analytics
note: White-box discrete-event simulator for provisioning caching scheduling and pricing policies in cloud analytics; exactly the trace and simulator driven policy study the scope allows on one machine. Simulator is pure user-space Python

title: Dilu: Enabling GPU Resourcing-on-Demand for Serverless DL Serving via Introspective Elasticity
note: GPU resourcing-on-demand for serverless DL serving - profiling plus 2D co-scaling; concern: paper uses a small GPU cluster but the elasticity mechanism is per-GPU and can be scaled to one A5000

title: Kairox: Adaptive GPU-CPU Hybrid LLM Inference via Online Neuron Balancing
note: Textbook fit: a llama.cpp-derived hybrid GPU+CPU engine that dynamically rebalances hot/cold FFN neuron groups between a single GPU and host CPU - 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM + 16 cores is the target hardware class

title: Blox: A Modular Toolkit for Deep Learning Schedulers
note: Explicitly a simulator-plus-toolkit for DL cluster scheduling policies, validated by reproducing prior schedulers from traces. Cluster behaviour is simulated, so no multi-node hardware is needed and new policies are cheap to prototype - a near-ideal 10-week improvement target
